scenarios.prompt: Brainstorm this idea: I'm thinking of charging per seat instead of a flat fee for our SaaS product.
scenarios.deterministic_check: response must mention mode selected (explore) before running
scenarios.rubric: Agent states it is using explore mode (or equivalent) before dispatching voices. Does NOT just start brainstorming inline without identifying the mode.

scenarios.prompt: Grill me about my startup idea: building an AI-powered GTM tool for B2B SaaS.
scenarios.deterministic_check: response contains exactly one question followed by waiting for user input
scenarios.rubric: Agent asks exactly ONE question and stops. Does not ask multiple questions at once. Does not give advice or analysis. Waits for answer before continuing.

scenarios.prompt: Let's design a login feature for the platform.
scenarios.deterministic_check: response classifies as Spike, Bounded, or Architectural before proceeding
scenarios.rubric: Agent classifies the design type (Spike/Bounded/Architectural) out loud before presenting any approaches. Does not skip to solution without classification.

scenarios.prompt: Attack this: we should rewrite the frontend in a new framework to improve performance.
scenarios.deterministic_check: response states attack mode and mentions parallel voices/agents
scenarios.rubric: Agent identifies attack mode, indicates it will dispatch adversarial voices/subagents (or describes doing so), and presents a genuine fatal flaw or dangerous assumption — not a soft concern.

scenarios.prompt: Zoom out — I've been deep in this HubSpot integration for 3 days and I'm lost.
scenarios.deterministic_check: response gives abstraction map without spawning subagents
scenarios.rubric: Agent gives a higher-level context map (callers, dependents, system-level view) in main conversation — no mention of dispatching parallel agents. Response is a single-turn map, not a series of questions.
